references.text: Moses asks to see God's glory as a sign that he has found favor in God's eyes; the same expression 'find favor in your eyes' is used.
Moses asks for signs from God to confirm his calling, just as Gideon does here.
Gideon asks for further signs with the fleece, continuing his desire for confirmation from God.
Saul waits for a sign before acting, following a similar pattern of seeking confirmation from God.
The Lord offers King Ahaz a sign, reflecting the same theme of divine confirmation through signs.
Hezekiah asks for a sign as confirmation of God's promise of healing.
The Pharisees ask Jesus for a sign; the theme of seeking divine confirmation continues in the New Testament.
